label: neiso53 winter fuelsec coldsnap
definition: G-24 NEISO winter fuel-security adoption on the neiso-50 base: three real ISO-NE winter mechanisms turned on together - gas cold-snap availability derate (TDFOR) + Component A oil-inventory budget + Component B fuel-secure must-run (WRP/IEP/OFSA + NERC Winter Storm Elliott). On 2023-2025 they are DORMANT on every scored metric (C3c/C5b unmoved, prices byte-near-identical to the ablation twin): the ample NEISO winter fleet never goes reserve-short under a <=13%-on-8-hours derate and the dual-fuel oil-parity cap (~$258) holds, so Component A never binds. Component B does commit the immaterial fuel-secure COAL fleet on cold days (<0.3% ISO load, reported-not-gated, rule 20 v2.1). Adopted for FORWARD faithfulness (rule 1: real, forward-responsive structure stays in even when the backcast residual does not move; binds in colder forecast years). Same determination as neiso-50 (CALIBRATED-WITH-CAVEATS). Refutes the hypothesis that a missing winter mechanism drives the C3c/C5b residual - that is a NEISO winter capacity-adequacy / scarcity-price-formation gap.
market_story: The NEISO winter fuel-security stack (cold-snap gas derate + oil-inventory budget + fuel-secure must-run) is structurally faithful but DORMANT on every scored 2023-2025 metric: vs the zero-mechanism twin, C3c stays 0h >$300 (max ~$258, oil-parity cap), 2025 storage moves 0.697->0.715 TWh (+2.6%), winter oil +0.8%, Component A oil budget never approached (~3.3 of 9.79 M MMBtu/month). Component B does commit the tiny fuel-secure COAL fleet on cold days (D-2 forced 0.35/0.23/0.02 vs 0.0 in the twin) but COAL is <0.3% of ISO load - reported-not-gated. The C3c tail / C5b storage residual is a capacity-adequacy / price-formation gap, not a fuel-security-mechanism gap - the mechanisms are kept on for the colder forecast years they would bind in, not to move this backcast.
